'''Narra Mesyne''' was a [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]] [[Special Enforcement Officer/Legends|Special Enforcement Officer]] active during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. While tracking down a known criminal she assumed the alias of Miraj in order to get closer to her target.

==Biography==
Narra was assigned to apprehend notorious criminal [[Kaylo NaKuda]]. In order to get close to her quarry she assumed the alias of Miraj, an up-and-coming racer who rapidly became famous in [[The Pit/Legends|The Pit]], a [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop racer]]&ndash;oriented [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] located on [[Stend VI]]. NaKuda owned a garage next to The Pit which Narra hoped to get closer to by rising through the ranks of [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] racers.

==Personality and traits==
Narra was shrewd and used the blatant sexism within the swoop-racing culture against her opponents. Her favorite tactic was to let her opponents think that victory would be theirs before accelerating past them at the last moment. While racing she would wear a tinted racing helmet, so her opponents would be shocked after losing a race to her for her to reveal that she was actually a beautiful woman. She had long dark hair with lighter highlighted bangs. In addition she often wore large earrings.

==Skills and abilities==
As a swoop racer Narra was skilled but not exceptional compared to other swoop racers on the track. As a [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Ranger]] she was highly skilled at espionage and investigations as well as law-enforcement tactics and intimidation.

In combat she was skilled with both [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee]]; however, she was only average at hand-to-hand combat.

==Equipment==
As Miraj, Narra rode a modified [[Aratech Repulsor Company/Legends|Aratech]] [[74-Z speeder bike/Legends|74-Z speeder bike]] that was painted white and silver which she called ''Wraith''.

She carried a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and wore [[camo scout armor]] that helped her move about unseen if she desired.

==Behind the scenes==
Nara Mesyne, also known as Miraj, was designed by [[Paul Danner]] and [[Bill Smith]] for ''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]'', a supplement for [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]] that was published by [[West End Games]] in [[1997]].

Nara Mesyne was designed as either a potential ally or enemy for the players depending on whether the players wanted to bring Kaylo NaKuda and his slaving empire or were hired by NaKuda to discover who had been attempting to spy on him.
